overall_summary: Geopolitical relief is lifting market sentiment today after Israel and Hezbollah renewed their ceasefire, allowing more oil to flow through the Strait of Hormuz. With the Fed on hold and steady U.S. data, risk assets like crypto are finding a constructive backdrop. Overall the tone feels cautiously optimistic for digital assets.

items.title: Fed Holds Rates Steady at 3.5-3.75% Range
items.summary: The Federal Reserve kept interest rates unchanged in its latest decision, citing solid economic activity amid Middle East uncertainty. Markets had fully expected the hold, with the committee noting steady job gains and strong productivity. Traders should watch for any shifts in dot plot projections or guidance on future cuts, as this keeps policy restrictive and supports a stronger dollar environment.
items.impact: Limits near-term rate cut bets, supporting USD and pressuring risk assets like Bitcoin.

items.title: US Initial Jobless Claims Ease to 226K
items.summary: Weekly jobless claims fell slightly to 226,000 for the week ending June 13, coming in just above the 225,000 forecast. The labor market remains stable overall despite some seasonal volatility. Traders care because persistent low claims signal resilience in employment, reducing recession fears but also keeping inflation concerns alive for the Fed.
items.impact: Reinforces soft landing narrative, mixed for Bitcoin as it supports equities but delays easing hopes.

items.title: S&P Global US Composite PMI Flash at 51.5
items.summary: The flash composite PMI for June came in at 51.5, indicating modest private sector expansion with manufacturing holding up better than services. Input costs rose sharply due to energy and supply issues. Traders should note this as a gauge of growth momentum heading into summer, with any further softening potentially weighing on risk sentiment.
items.impact: Signals steady but not accelerating growth, neutral to slightly cautious for markets amid sticky inflation signals.

items.title: Israel, Hezbollah Agree to Renewed Ceasefire in Lebanon
items.summary: Israel and Hezbollah have agreed to a ceasefire starting Friday afternoon, mediated by the US, Qatar, and Iran, after overnight clashes killed dozens. The deal comes amid efforts to stabilize the region following the broader US-Iran conflict. Traders should watch this as reduced escalation risk in the Middle East supports risk assets and helps ease oil supply concerns.
items.impact: Eases immediate war fears, supports risk-on sentiment and lower oil volatility.

items.title: US-Iran Talks Postponed Amid Lebanon Fighting
items.summary: Planned technical talks between the US and Iran in Switzerland were postponed after fresh Israel-Hezbollah clashes threatened the fragile interim deal signed earlier this week. US envoy Steve Witkoff is still traveling, but initial meetings are delayed as parties work to get negotiations back on track within the 60-day window. Traders care because ongoing uncertainty around the Iran deal keeps oil market and geopolitical risk premiums elevated.
items.impact: Prolongs uncertainty, limits immediate bullish relief for markets.

items.title: Oil Shipments Rise Through Strait of Hormuz Post-Deal
items.summary: Commercial traffic through the Strait of Hormuz is picking up after the recent US-Iran memorandum reopened the waterway, though questions linger over Iranian transit terms and fees. Brent crude is set for an 8% weekly drop as markets price in better supply flow. Traders should note this as a key de-escalation signal that could further pressure oil prices lower and support broader risk assets.
items.impact: Reduces energy shock risk, bullish for equities and crypto via lower inflation pressure.
